tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The decorator resolves allowed targets and checks arg.unit.is_equivalent until one matches (astropy/units/decorators.py:27-39,52-70). is_equivalent normalizes equivalencies and resolves the other Unit (astropy/units/core.py:984-1003). These are per-call operations, but physical type IDs are cached (astropy/units/core.py:675-684); the source does not establish a numeric overhead or an expensive decomposition on every invocation. Registry copying is avoided when equivalencies are empty (astropy/units/decorators.py:307-313).

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Each binary table serialization allocates a BytesIO, appends converter output, and base64-encodes its complete contents (astropy/io/votable/tree.py:3460-3495). The test setups additionally create an output BytesIO and parse it after serialization, and test_null_integer_binary serializes again (astropy/io/votable/tests/test_vo.py:748-805). This entails buffer allocation and encoding work, but these sources do not measure the cost or establish that constructing BytesIO dominates it; class setup is not run once per inherited test.

checked_claims.claim: All arithmetic and output formats retain the two-part precision
checked_claims.reason: The multi-component path preserves the remainder but the single-unit format explicitly adds jd1+jd2; universal guarantee is too broad.

material_errors: The multi-component path preserves the remainder but the single-unit format explicitly adds jd1+jd2; universal guarantee is too broad.
tasks.notes: Source read directly; no repository code executed. Performance and intent claims limited to source evidence.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The two parts retain small fractional contributions alongside large day counts. set_jds separates years/days from hour/minute/second terms and normalizes them using day_frac (astropy/time/formats.py:2424-2428), whose result is an integer and fractional remainder (astropy/time/utils.py:19-27). Multi-component output uses two_sum and its remainder before extracting hours, minutes, and seconds (astropy/time/formats.py:2460-2470). This reduces precision loss; it does not guarantee exactness in every output format, since single-unit output sums the two parts (astropy/time/formats.py:2440-2453).

checked_claims.claim: binoutput converts values according to self.format
checked_claims.reason: The format configures size and binary parsing; output itself only swaps and emits existing value bytes, not a dtype cast.

material_errors: The format configures size and binary parsing; output itself only swaps and emits existing value bytes, not a dtype cast.
tasks.notes: Source read directly; no repository code executed. Performance and intent claims limited to source evidence.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: FloatComplex declares format="c8", a pair of single-precision components (astropy/io/votable/converters.py:1097-1103). Numeric initialization derives an 8-byte size and >c8 binary-read dtype (astropy/io/votable/converters.py:706-720). The inherited binoutput returns null bytes for a mask; otherwise it ensures big-endian byte order and calls value.tobytes() (astropy/io/votable/converters.py:823-828). It relies on the incoming NumPy value having the appropriate dtype; binoutput does not itself cast through self.format.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The function returns a coordinate frame, not a bare CartesianDifferential. It transforms both inputs to ICRS, attaches the reference Cartesian differentials to the original ICRS position, then transforms that coordinate to velocity_reference when preserve_observer_frame is False. The returned frame uses CartesianRepresentation and CartesianDifferential (astropy/coordinates/spectral_coordinate.py:103-124). Its differential describes motion co-moving with the reference while retaining the original spatial location (astropy/coordinates/spectral_coordinate.py:80-87).
